correction.originalCritique: Strongest feature: The diagnostic presents a crisp dilemma: independently justificatory desert makes the account mixed, while nonjustificatory desert becomes dispensable, directly challenging the coherence of “consequentialist desert.” Principal limitation: The two branches compress possible derivative, constitutive, expressive, or rule-internal roles through which desert terminology might operate within an ultimately consequentialist institutional design. Live burden: The skeptic must show that these intermediate roles either secretly introduce backward-looking justification or contribute nothing unavailable through clearer forward-looking concepts and practices. Locked score: The very-strong band reflects exceptional responsiveness, logical clarity, precise targeting, strong charity, and major leverage against the opposing institutional account, with only a bounded gap concerning sophisticated rule-consequentialist constructions of desert.
